poster.venue: The Lancet Digital Health – AI in Clinical Medicine Symposium

brief.title: Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Decision-Making: Performance, Safety, and Implementation Gaps
brief.one_liner: A synthesis of current evidence on AI-assisted clinical decision support systems, highlighting diagnostic accuracy gains, safety considerations, and the translational gap from research to bedside deployment.
brief.goal: Viewers should understand the current state of AI in clinical decision-making — where it excels, where risks remain, and what steps are needed to bridge the implementation gap in real-world healthcare settings.

sections.title: Background & Motivation
sections.objective: Establish why AI-based clinical decision support is a critical area of digital health research and frame the scope of the review.

sections.title: Diagnostic Performance of AI Systems
sections.objective: Present key accuracy and sensitivity metrics comparing AI-assisted versus standard clinical workflows across major disease domains.

sections.title: Safety, Bias, and Health Equity
sections.objective: Highlight evidence on algorithmic bias, patient safety events, and disparities across demographic groups.

sections.title: The Translational Implementation Gap
sections.objective: Quantify how few validated AI tools reach routine clinical use and identify the primary barriers.

sections.title: Recommendations & Future Directions
sections.objective: Summarize actionable steps for researchers, clinicians, and policymakers to accelerate safe AI adoption.
